quarterly_data.signal: Keel's 10-K: its Infrastructure Assets operate ASIC miners contributing hashrate to Mining Pools under Full Pay Per Share (FPPS) arrangements, with fees paid daily in Bitcoin; during fiscal 2025 one Mining Pool operator accounted for 88% of total revenue. It participates in a single Mining Pool, the Foundry Pool, which has the right to unilaterally modify the service agreement, including the payout methodology or pool fees. As of December 31, 2025 it operated 113,649 ASIC miners with total hashrate of 14.8 EH/s, and as of March 27, 2026 Bitcoin Mining was continuing at all of its sites.
quarterly_data.figure: One pool operator 88% of revenue (fiscal 2025); 113,649 ASIC miners, 14.8 EH/s (December 31, 2025)

quarterly_data.signal: Keel's 10-K mining KPIs (continuing operations): Bitcoin earned through Bitcoin Mining 2,008 in fiscal 2025 versus 1,992 in 2024 (+1%), plus 46 Bitcoin received through hosting revenue; cost per kWh $0.049 versus $0.047; Average Watts/Average TH efficiency 18 versus 25, installed Watts/TH efficiency 19 versus 21. Mining power came from Hydro-Quebec, Hydro-Magog, Hydro-Sherbrooke and the City of Baie-Comeau in Quebec, the Grant County Power Utility District in Washington, and Stronghold and the PJM Interconnection merchant market in Pennsylvania. Fiscal 2025 costs include $9.2 million of customs duties following a U.S. Customs and Border Protection determination on Miners it imported in 2021.
quarterly_data.figure: 2,008 Bitcoin earned (fiscal 2025, +1%); $0.049 per kWh; 18 Watts/TH average efficiency

quarterly_data.signal: Keel's 10-K: in the first quarter of 2024 the company ordered 19,369 Bitmain T21 Miners, 3,975 Bitmain S21 Miners and 762 Bitmain S21 Hydro Miners for $51,285, $13,608 and $4,338 (in thousands) respectively, with deliveries scheduled from April 2024 to November 2024; in November 2024 it amended the order, upgrading 12,853 Bitmain T21 Miners to 12,853 S21 Pro Miners for $22,654. As of December 31, 2025 all Miners on the order were received, and miner purchase order deposits were nil versus $34,791 a year earlier.
quarterly_data.figure: 19,369 T21 + 3,975 S21 + 762 S21 Hydro Bitmain miners ($51,285 / $13,608 / $4,338 thousand); 12,853 upgraded to S21 Pro for $22,654 thousand

quarterly_data.signal: Keel's 10-K: as part of its strategic shift toward HPC/AI infrastructure in North America it discontinued all operations in Argentina and agreed to divest all operations in Argentina and Paraguay, expecting the divestitures and wind-downs to reduce go-forward capital commitments by $22 million. Energy provider GMSA halted electricity supply to its 58 MW Rio Cuarto, Argentina Bitcoin data center on May 12, 2025; the plant was shut down and abandoned by September 30, 2025. The Paso Pe, Paraguay Bitcoin data center was classified as held for sale, and on March 17, 2025 it sold its 200 MW Bitcoin data center under development in Yguazu, Paraguay to HIVE Digital Technologies. The discontinued Argentina and Paraguay operations generated revenues of $58,713 thousand in fiscal 2025 (Argentina $10,612, Paraguay $48,101).
quarterly_data.figure: Rio Cuarto 58 MW abandoned; Yguazu 200 MW sold to HIVE; discontinued Latin America revenue $58,713 thousand (fiscal 2025)

quarterly_data.signal: Keel's 10-K revenue by country (in thousands): United States $116,386 in fiscal 2025 versus $16,500 in 2024 and $11,466 in 2023; Canada $112,890 versus $116,774 and $108,934.

Keel's 10-K: it has engaged first-tier companies, including ASG, CBRE, Consertus, Corgan, Gensler, Langan, Syska Hennessy Group, Turner Construction Company, Vertiv and WWT, to access deep, domain-specific expertise at each development stage, while retaining strategic control over site selection, power procurement, capital allocation and customer relationships; it says this mitigates execution risk while it builds permanent internal capabilities and positions it to internalize more of the development value chain over time.
